record.paper_title: Open Questions in High Energy Spin Physics
record.context_brief: Strange and anti-strange quarks in the nucleon
record.original_question: Determine whether strange quarks s and anti-strange quarks s̄ in the nucleon have significantly different spatial and momentum distributions. C-even observables add s and s̄ contributions, while parity-violating electron scattering is sensitive to C-odd quantities such as strange magnetization and charge radius, and neutrino dimuon production can in principle separate s and s̄ momentum distributions. The open question is whether experiments can show significant s–s̄ differences.

evidence.quote: What are the properties of the s and s̄ quarks in the nucleon?
The next round of experiments should tell us whether s and s̄ quarks in the nucleon have significantly different spatial distributions.
Parity violating (xF3) dimuon production in neutrino DIS can, in principle, separate s and s̄ momentum distributions. Present data are not accurate enough to differentiate s and s̄.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the nucleon described in QCD as a bound state containing, among its sea quarks, strange quarks s and antistrange quarks s̄. Define the unpolarized strange and antistrange parton distribution functions s(x,Q²) and s̄(x,Q²), as well as C-odd combinations such as the strange contribution to the magnetic form factor (strange magnetization) and the strange charge radius of the nucleon, which are sensitive to the difference between s and s̄ contributions (parity-violating elastic electron–nucleon scattering probes such C-odd quantities, while neutrino-induced charged-current dimuon production probes ∫ x[s(x)−s̄(x)]dx).

Determine whether the s and s̄ distributions in the nucleon differ significantly:
(a) Is the momentum asymmetry ∫₀¹ x[s(x,Q²) − s̄(x,Q²)] dx nonzero at a statistically significant level, and what is its sign and magnitude?
(b) Do s and s̄ have significantly different spatial distributions inside the nucleon, as reflected in nonzero strange electromagnetic form factors (strange magnetic moment μ_s and strange charge radius ⟨r²⟩_s)?

Provide a quantitative determination of these C-odd s−s̄ observables from experiment.
artifact.status_search_result: Experimental measurements have constrained but not definitively resolved the s−s̄ asymmetry. NuTeV dimuon analyses at NLO yielded a positive strange momentum asymmetry at only ~1.6σ significance, and global PDF fits (CT, NNPDF, MSHT) still find s(x)−s̄(x) consistent with zero within sizeable uncertainties. Parity-violating electron scattering experiments (HAPPEX, G0, Qweak) have constrained the strange magnetic moment and charge radius to be small and consistent with zero. Thus the question of a significant s–s̄ difference remains only partially answered.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the Nucleon Strange-Antistrange Asymmetry at NLO from NuTeV Dimuon Data
status_evidence.snippet: Found a positive strange asymmetry with a significance of 1.6 sigma.
status_evidence.claim: NuTeV dimuon analysis finds nonzero s−s̄ momentum asymmetry only at ~1.6σ, not yet conclusive.

status_evidence.title: Determining the strange and antistrange quark distributions of the nucleon (arXiv:1104.5592)
status_evidence.snippet: Two phenomenological models give opposite predictions for s−s̄ asymmetry; coming experiments likely able to distinguish.
status_evidence.claim: The shape and size of s(x)−s̄(x) is not yet determined and remains under active phenomenological study.

status_evidence.title: Form factors and other measures of strangeness in the nucleon (arXiv:0711.4304)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews strange form factors of the nucleon.
status_evidence.claim: Parity-violating electron scattering has constrained but not yet definitively established nonzero strange magnetic moment and charge radius.
